name: thinness

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Thinness is the Celtic belief that reality is not the same everywhere. Common reality is solid and opaque. But some places grow thin, and the Otherworld lies close by. Fairy trees that grow alone in a rocky field count as such places. Bogs where people can be lost and drowned count too. Islands that seem far or near as the air shifts also count. There are also thin times in the year. These are turning points when Otherworld forces may cross into this world. Or the living may stumble into the Other. Each day has a thin moment at twilight. Two days each year grow so thin that the two worlds collide. These are the feast of Beltane and the feast of Samhain. Beltane falls on the first day of May. Samhain falls on the first day of November. The belief in thinness may link to shape-shifting. That is the power to change the body into an animal, a plant, or a fog.

okr.objective: Record the Celtic notion of thin places and thin times.
key_results: Reality has thin places where the Otherworld is near
Fairy trees, bogs, and distant islands count as thin places
Twilight is a thin time on every day
Beltane and Samhain are the days when the worlds collide
